---
title: "Terminals"
subtitle: "A real bash in a real Linux VM — right inside your page."
quarto-os:
  vm:
    setup: |
      mkdir -p ~/playground
      cd ~/playground
      printf 'cherries\napples\nbananas\napples\n' > fruits.txt
      printf 'import sys\nprint("Python", sys.version.split()[0], "says hi!")\n' > hello.py
---

A terminal window runs `bash` in a Debian Linux VM that lives entirely in your browser
(powered by [CheerpX](https://cheerpx.io)). The first terminal on the page boots the VM —
that takes a few seconds on the first visit while the engine and disk blocks are
downloaded. All terminals on a page share **one** VM.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## What's in this VM?
The default disk is Debian (i386) with `bash`, `git`, `python3`, `nano`, `vim`, `less`,
`grep`, `sed`, `awk` and the usual coreutils. The user is `user` with the home directory
`/home/user` (`~`). There is **no network** inside the VM, so `apt install` or
`pip install` won't work. This page's front matter prepares a `~/playground` folder with
two files using `quarto-os: vm: setup:`.
:::

## Your first terminal

A terminal is a window with `app="terminal"`. Give it an `#id` so snippets can target it:

````markdown
::: {#shell .os-window app="terminal" title="bash" height="300px" cwd="~/playground"}
:::
````

::: {#shell .os-window app="terminal" title="bash" height="300px" cwd="~/playground"}
:::

### Clickable run snippets

Add `.os-run` to inline code or a code block and it becomes clickable: a click types the
text into the terminal and presses <kbd>Enter</kbd>. Try them — they all go to the
terminal above (`target="shell"`):

- List the files: `ls -la`{.os-run target="shell"}
- Count the lines: `wc -l fruits.txt`{.os-run target="shell"}
- Sort and de-duplicate: `sort fruits.txt | uniq -c`{.os-run target="shell"}
- Run Python: `python3 hello.py`{.os-run target="shell"}

A code block with several lines sends them one after another:

```{.bash .os-run target="shell"}
echo "durian" >> fruits.txt
sort -u fruits.txt
```

This is the Markdown for the snippets above:

````markdown
- List the files: `ls -la`{.os-run target="shell"}

```{.bash .os-run target="shell"}
echo "durian" >> fruits.txt
sort -u fruits.txt
```
````

::: {.callout-tip}
Snippets are a great way to let beginners follow along without typos — but it's a real
shell, so encourage them to type the next command themselves.
:::

## Starting directory and commands: `cwd` & `run`

`cwd` sets the directory the shell starts in, and `run` types a command as soon as the shell
is ready (separate several commands with `;`). Here we use the shortcode form, which is
handy when you don't need an id:

```markdown
{{{< os terminal title="python3 — playground" cwd="~/playground" run="python3 hello.py; python3 -c 'print(6 * 7)'" height="200px" >}}}
```

{{< os terminal title="python3 — playground" cwd="~/playground" run="python3 hello.py; python3 -c 'print(6 * 7)'" height="200px" >}}

## Two terminals, one machine

Every terminal on a page is a separate shell **on the same VM**, so they see the same files and
processes. Start a "chat" that the right terminal follows with `tail -f`, then write to it
from the left:

::: {.win-row .cols-2}

::: {#left .os-window app="terminal" title="left" height="260px" cwd="~"}
:::

::: {#right .os-window app="terminal" title="right" height="260px" theme="dark" cwd="~"}
:::

:::

1. Right: `touch /tmp/chat.log; tail -f /tmp/chat.log`{.os-run target="right"}
2. Left: `echo "left: hello, right!" >> /tmp/chat.log`{.os-run target="left"}
3. Left: `echo "left: we share one VM" >> /tmp/chat.log`{.os-run target="left"}
4. Left: `ps -e | grep tail`{.os-run target="left"} — the left shell sees the right one's process

Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> in the right terminal to stop `tail`.

````markdown
::: {.win-row .cols-2}

::: {#left .os-window app="terminal" title="left" height="260px"}
:::

::: {#right .os-window app="terminal" title="right" height="260px" theme="dark"}
:::

:::

Right: `tail -f /tmp/chat.log`{.os-run target="right"}
````

## Snippets without a target

Without `target`, a snippet goes to the terminal you used (focused) most recently. Click
into one of the terminals above, then click: `uname -a; whoami; pwd`{.os-run}

If there is no terminal yet, a new floating terminal opens over the page. You can also
open one yourself with a launch button — each click opens a new instance, which you can
drag around and close:

[Open a floating terminal]{.os-launch app="terminal" title="floating bash" cwd="~/playground" width=560 height=320}

```markdown
[Open a floating terminal]{.os-launch app="terminal" title="floating bash" cwd="~/playground"}
```

## Keyboard & clipboard

- The terminal is a full [xterm.js](https://xtermjs.org) terminal: colors, cursor keys, tab
  completion, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd>, full-screen programs like `nano`, `vim` and `less`.
- Copy and paste work with your browser's usual shortcuts.
- Everything resets when you reload the page — unless the document sets
  `quarto-os: vm: persist: true`.
